Name: Gregory the Great
Summary: Roman monk who became pope in 590 and led the church in Rome through plague, famine and Lombard invasion.
Contribution: He reformed church administration, cared for the poor of Rome, wrote influential pastoral guidance, sent the mission to England, and is traditionally associated with the chant that bears his name.
Testimony: He preferred the monastic life and described the papal office as a burden of service, taking it up out of obedience rather than ambition.
